_meta.note: sarcasm and self_deprecation are classified here for taxonomy/co-occurrence purposes only; their deep target/trigger analyses are owned by other workers and not duplicated here.
_meta.abstraction_rule: OBSERVED/INFERRED structural abstraction only; no verbatim punchlines stored anywhere in this file.

structure: another character makes a statement or takes an action
speaker replies using words that literally mean the opposite of, or overstate, the sincere response
tone/context signals the literal meaning is not intended, producing a mocking or needling effect
context is grounded in an ordinary or realistic circumstance
speaker introduces a surreal, illogical, or physically/socially impossible element
no attempt is made to reconcile the absurd element with reality
response contains genuinely absurd, exaggerated, or biting content
delivery/framing is flat, sincere-sounding, or matter-of-fact with no signal of amusement
the contrast between wild content and flat delivery is the mechanism itself
context presents a real but bounded problem, feeling, or scale
speaker inflates the scope, stakes, or numbers well past realistic proportion
the gap between real and stated magnitude produces the comic effect
context poses a direct, often uncomfortable or probing question or topic
speaker responds with a joke instead of substantive engagement
the topic is avoided while appearing to have been addressed
context presents an event that is emotionally or practically significant
speaker describes it in flat, minimizing, or dismissive terms
the mismatch between severity and description produces the comic effect
two elements (tone, register, content, formality) are juxtaposed within the same response
the elements are individually plausible but clash against one another
the unresolved clash, rather than any resolution, is the joke
speaker's opening words build toward an expected direction or conclusion
speaker abruptly pivots to an unrelated or contradictory ending
the swerve, not the content of either half alone, creates the surprise
context presents a scenario that seems to call for an obvious response
speaker poses a rhetorical question or device instead of answering directly
the rhetorical framing itself carries the comic point (mock incredulity, feigned disbelief)
a detail or phrase is established earlier within the given context window
speaker's response re-invokes that same detail in a new frame
recognition of the repetition, not the content alone, produces the humor
context creates social tension, an unanswerable question, or an uncomfortable silence
speaker's response fills the gap without resolving the discomfort
the discomfort itself, made visible rather than smoothed over, is the source of humor
context or the speaker's own words contain a term with two or more possible meanings, or a similar-sounding alternative
speaker's response activates the secondary or homophonic meaning
recognizing both meanings at once is what produces the humor
context includes a person, object, or situation that needs describing
speaker maps it onto an incongruous domain via simile, metaphor, or analogy
the distance between the two domains generates the humor
context surfaces a mundane or specific situation
speaker generalizes it into a broader pattern about people, relationships, or life
the generalization is delivered as a shared, recognizable truth
a stated expectation or norm is established by the context
the actual outcome, or the speaker's own framing, directly contradicts that expectation
the contradiction itself, not a direct insult, generates the humor
context presents the speaker in a flattering, high-stakes, or neutral light
speaker reframes the situation to lower his own status, competence, or worth
speaker becomes the target of the joke rather than anyone else
the circumstance established by context is inherently embarrassing, ironic, or ill-timed
speaker's response simply describes, acknowledges, or reacts to the circumstance
no wordplay or twist is needed; the situation itself supplies the comedy
context involves the act of talking, storytelling, or a conversational convention itself
speaker comments on the conversation, the joke, or the narrative frame rather than its content
breaking frame (acknowledging the 'bit', the audience, or the format) creates the effect
speaker begins with one comic claim or example
each subsequent clause or sentence ratchets the claim further in severity, quantity, or absurdity
the joke peaks with the final, most extreme item in the sequence
a banter/teasing exchange is already underway between speaker and another character
speaker's line extends, volleys, or one-ups the previous line in the same playful register
the humor depends on the back-and-forth rhythm, not on any single line standing alone
another speaker uses a figurative, idiomatic, or rhetorical phrase
speaker responds by treating the phrase as though it means exactly what it literally says
the literal reading exposes an absurdity or unintended meaning hidden in the phrase
context or the early part of the response sets up one role, outcome, or expectation
the ending flips that role, outcome, or expectation, often onto the speaker or another party
the flip recontextualizes everything said before it
